references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Zeno’s Paradoxes
references.support: Scholarly discussion of Aristotle’s mediated report of the Arrow argument and a modern at-at response; §3.3 (Arrow) and §3.4 (Stadium) consulted, not the full entry.

references.title: Aristotle, Physics, Book VI, chapter 9, trans. R. P. Hardie and R. K. Gaye
references.support: Primary ancient testimony: Physics VI.9 at 239b5–9 and 239b30–33 reports Zeno’s Arrow argument and Aristotle’s objection; the same chapter reports the Stadium. Relevant passages read in the Hardie–Gaye translation; the online page does not specify the edition date.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Zeno of Elea
references.support: Historical context for Zeno’s fifth-century BCE period and the indirect transmission and reconstruction of the Arrow from Aristotle’s testimony; §§1 and 2.2.3 consulted, not the full entry.

references.title: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, §3.2, “Instantaneous Velocity and Speed”
references.support: Textbook support for defining instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocity as elapsed time approaches zero; §3.2 read. This provides calculus context, not an interpretation of Zeno.
